reason: Read with the 1474 print at hand, the abbreviated orations ('Co(m)pl(enda)', 'sollempnitate', 'concede p(ro)picius') and the worn Romans lines could be expanded and checked, and the faint red mark above canvas 1 was read as the folio number cxvij rather than 'cc xvij'.
sources: Missale Romanum, Mediolani 1474, ed. R. Lippe, vol. 1, HBS 17 (1899), pp. 406-408, In natali plurimorum apostolorum, MDZ bsb12035531 scans 440-442, https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb12035531?page=440
Munich, BSB, Clm 7901, Kaisheim Cistercian missal, 1531, canvases 315, 351, 381, https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb00103566?page=315
Missale Eboracense (ed. 1874), secret Debitum of St Thomas, and H. A. Wilson, The Gelasian Sacramentary (1894), Conserva: search snippets only
text:
F-e0vk (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 214). Source-assisted reading, 31 October 2026, made with the Missale Romanum, Milan 1474 (ed. Lippe, vol. 1, pp. 406-408) at hand. A research reader reread on the native images canvas 1 column a in full, the middle of canvas 0 column b, the faded rubric before Eph 1:3 and the loose strips. An independent checker reread canvas 0 column a lines 1-12 and the end of Eph 2 on canvas 1 column b on the image before opening the source. The rest of canvas 1 column b and of canvas 0 column a rests on the image-only first reading, checked against the overview and the edition. The torn bands are unread. Not a verified transcription.
Conventions: expansions in ( ), lost or supplied text in [ ], ? doubtful, / line break, [red] rubric. Boxes are left,top,right,bottom in native pixels (4912 x 7360). Reading order: canvas 1 (original recto, f. cxvij) then canvas 0 (f. cxvij verso).
